title: A Price War Is Making Top AI Cheaper
hook: OpenAI and Anthropic are cutting prices as cheaper Chinese models win users. Competition, not generosity, is what pushes good AI within reach of ordinary budgets.
key_points: Ars Technica reports US labs released cheaper models under pressure from Chinese rivals.
The trigger is competition: capable low-cost models make premium pricing hard to defend.
For everyday users this shows up as more free tiers and cheaper paid plans.
Price is not quality — a cheaper model can be plenty for writing, summarizing, and Q&A.
Shop the way you would for any service: try the free tier before you subscribe.
content_html: The two best-known American AI labs, OpenAI and Anthropic, have been cutting prices — and Ars Technica reports the reason is competition rather than charity. Chinese rivals have been shipping capable models at far lower prices, and once a good-enough model is cheap, charging a premium for the frontier gets harder.
extra_html: This is ordinary market behavior arriving in a market that had felt immune to it. For you, the effect is practical: more generous free tiers, cheaper paid plans, and less reason to lock yourself into a subscription before you know you need one. The habit worth keeping is the same as for any service — start on the free tier, notice whether you actually hit its limits, and only then pay. A model's price tag says more about the company's position in this fight than about whether it can help you draft an email.

related.title: Free vs Paid Tools
related.hook: The free tier is enough for most people most of the time. Paid plans mostly buy you the smarter model, higher limits, and stronger privacy — useful only if you'll actually use them.

related.title: China's Free-to-Download Models Are Closing the Gap
related.hook: A Chinese lab's openly downloadable model reportedly rivals the top US models at some security tasks — a sign the distance between open AI and the frontier is shrinking fast.

related.title: Why China Gives Away Its Best AI Models
related.hook: Moonshot's Kimi K3 reportedly matches top US systems at a fraction of the cost — and you can just download it. Giving the model away isn't charity; it's strategy.

flashcards.prompt: According to the report, what pushed OpenAI and Anthropic to cut prices?

choices.text: Competition from cheaper Chinese models gaining ground
A new law capping what AI companies may charge
A drop in the number of people using chatbots

flashcards.explanation_html: The price cuts followed competitive pressure — capable low-cost rivals make premium pricing hard to sustain.

flashcards.prompt: Why shouldn't you assume the most expensive AI plan is the one you need?
flashcards.back_html: Price tracks market position, not your use case. For writing, summarizing, and everyday questions, a cheap or free tier is often enough — try it first.
